name: Online order return and refund at a mid-size retailer
summary: When an online shopper sends back an item, the retailer has to authorise the return, give the customer a prepaid label, receive the parcel at its distribution centre, check the item's condition, refund or exchange it and decide whether the item can be sold again. Customer service, warehouse associates, a refunds team and loss prevention each handle part of it, and the carrier and card issuer add their own delays. About a fifth of online sales came back in 2021, so the volume is large, and most of the customer's wait is the time before drop-off, carrier transit and the returns backlog in the warehouse. Errors come from mismatched parcels, inconsistent grading, fraud such as wardrobing or wrong items, and refund status calls while customers wait.

baseline.org_archetype: An online apparel and home goods retailer with about $300 million in online sales, its own distribution centre with a returns area, an in-house customer service team and a self-service returns portal linked to the order management system.
baseline.notes: One case is one return request (one or more items from one order). Returns are processed at the retailer's own distribution centre; refunds go to the original payment method.

unit_of_work: one return request for items from one online order
trigger: A customer asks to return items from a delivered online order, through the returns portal or customer service.
end_state: The refund is posted to the customer's account or an exchange order is created, and the item is restocked or staged for liquidation, vendor return or disposal; or the request is denied, refused after inspection or never shipped.

volume.seasonality: Highest in January after holiday sales (NRF expected 13.3% of 2020 holiday sales to come back) and lowest in late summer.

evidence.note: Online return rate of 20.8% (src1) applied to about 23,000 online orders a month for a retailer with $300 million in online sales and an average order of about $110 (author's assumption); January peak from src2.

produces.object: returned item back in sellable stock
returned item for liquidation, vendor return or disposal
refund, inventory adjustment and dispute records

evidence.note: Handles return requests and refund status contacts by phone, chat and email. Median $17.75. Loaded cost = BLS May 2021 median hourly wage x 1.45 (1.30 benefits from BLS ECEC December 2021 for retail trade, about 1.12 overhead by author estimate).

Approves policy exceptions and high-value refunds. Median $29.13. Loaded cost = BLS May 2021 median hourly wage x 1.45 (1.30 benefits from BLS ECEC December 2021 for retail trade, about 1.12 overhead by author estimate).

Unloads and scans return parcels at the dock. Median $17.74. Loaded cost = BLS May 2021 median hourly wage x 1.45 (1.30 benefits from BLS ECEC December 2021 for retail trade, about 1.12 overhead by author estimate).

Opens, matches, inspects and grades returned items. Laborers and Freight, Stock and Material Movers median $15.02. Loaded cost = BLS May 2021 median hourly wage x 1.45 (1.30 benefits from BLS ECEC December 2021 for retail trade, about 1.12 overhead by author estimate).

Researches unmatched parcels and decides failed-inspection cases. Median $26.37. Loaded cost = BLS May 2021 median hourly wage x 1.45 (1.30 benefits from BLS ECEC December 2021 for retail trade, about 1.12 overhead by author estimate).

Releases refunds and exchanges in the order management system in daily batches. Customer Service Representatives median $17.75, set slightly higher for back-office work. Loaded cost = BLS May 2021 median hourly wage x 1.45 (1.30 benefits from BLS ECEC December 2021 for retail trade, about 1.12 overhead by author estimate).

systems.name: Self-service returns portal (rules, labels, status emails)
Ecommerce platform and order management system
Warehouse management system with returns module
Customer service helpdesk (phone, chat, email tickets)
Returns fraud rules (built into the returns platform or OMS)
Handheld barcode scanners and packing stations

steps.name: Customer starts a return
steps.description: The customer decides to send back one or more items, usually for fit, appearance or damage, and either opens the self-service returns page from the order email or contacts customer service. The customer's own few minutes are not counted as staff time.

error.defect_description: Customer picks the wrong item or reason.

next.condition: contacts customer service by phone, chat or email

evidence.note: The return starts with a request and reason (src3) and needs the seller's authorisation (src8). The 72% portal share is the author's estimate for a mid-size retailer with a returns portal in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Portal checks eligibility and authorises
steps.description: The returns portal looks up the order, checks the return window, final-sale flags and item eligibility against the posted policy, and authorises the return automatically or sends the customer to customer service.

error.defect_description: Rule set wrongly allows a final-sale item.

control.basis: Retailer's posted return policy (window, condition, final sale); state disclosure laws such as California Civil Code 1723 require restrictions to be posted

next.condition: outside the rules: customer contacts customer service

evidence.note: Rule-based approval of eligibility (src3); return conditions and time limits (src6). Split is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Customer service handles the return request
steps.description: A customer service representative opens the order in the order system, checks the policy, asks for photos when damage is claimed, creates the return authorisation by hand and explains next steps; out-of-policy requests go to a supervisor.

error.defect_description: Authorisation created for the wrong item or quantity.

evidence.note: Handle times and queue waits are the author's estimate for phone, chat and email channels.

steps.name: Supervisor decides policy exception
steps.description: The customer service supervisor reviews the customer's history and order value and decides whether to allow a late or out-of-policy return as goodwill.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Customer service authority matrix: exceptions to the return policy need supervisor approval

evidence.note: Author's estimate of exception handling.

steps.name: Issue return label and authorisation
steps.description: The returns platform creates the return authorisation number and a prepaid carrier label or QR code and emails them to the customer with packing instructions.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Prepaid carrier return shipments (src5) and the authorisation step (src8).

steps.name: Customer packs and drops off the parcel
steps.description: The customer packs the item and drops it at a carrier location or schedules a pickup. Some customers never send the item, and the authorisation expires.

error.defect_description: Wrong item or missing item packed.

next.condition: label lost or expired: customer asks customer service for a new one

evidence.note: Customer delay before drop-off, the 4% who need a new label and the 7% not shipped are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Parcel in transit to the returns centre
steps.description: The carrier collects the parcel and moves it by ground service to the distribution centre; tracking scans update the returns portal so customer service and the customer can follow it.

error.defect_description: Parcel lost or damaged in transit.

next.condition: customer contacts customer service about the refund

evidence.note: Ground delivery takes 1 to 5 business days in the contiguous US (src5); converted to two to eight calendar days including weekends.

steps.name: Answer refund status contact
steps.description: A customer service representative takes a call, chat or email from a customer asking where the refund is, checks carrier tracking and the returns record, explains the timeline and sometimes escalates.

error.defect_description: Agent promises a refund date the warehouse cannot meet.

next.condition: customer disputes the charge with the card issuer

evidence.note: Share of returns that generate a status contact and handle time are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Receive and scan return parcels
steps.description: The receiving clerk unloads return parcels, often in a daily batch, scans each label into the warehouse system so the customer sees it as received, and stages the parcels in the returns area, where they wait for processing.

error.defect_description: Parcel scanned to the wrong authorisation.

evidence.note: Returns are usually processed after outbound orders, so they queue for days, longer after peak season; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Open parcel and match to the authorisation
steps.description: A returns associate opens the parcel at a returns station, scans the authorisation and item barcodes and checks that the item and quantity match what was authorised.

error.defect_description: Mismatch not noticed.

next.condition: no authorisation, wrong item or unreadable label

evidence.note: Inbound and inspection steps (src3). Times and mismatch rate are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Research unmatched return
steps.description: The returns team lead puts the parcel on the problem shelf and searches the order system by name, address or item to find the order, contacting customer service when the customer must be asked.

error.defect_description: Item credited to the wrong customer.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of problem-shelf handling.

steps.name: Inspect and grade the item
steps.description: The associate checks the item for wear, odour, stains, removed tags, missing parts and damage, compares it with the product record and grades it as new, open-box, damaged or not acceptable, photographing problems.

error.defect_description: Worn or wrong item graded as new.

control.basis: Return policy condition requirements checked before refund (unworn, tags attached, complete)

evidence.note: Inspection against policy and grading (src3); resellable condition (src6); quality check before return to inventory (src7). Times and fail rate are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Run fraud screening rules
steps.description: The returns platform or order system applies rules to the customer and return, such as return frequency, value, mismatched item, weight or shipping address, and holds suspicious refunds for review.

error.defect_description: Genuine fraud passes the rules.

control.basis: Loss prevention policy for return fraud screening

evidence.note: Return fraud cost $10.30 per $100 returned in 2021 and $5.90 in 2020 (src1, src2), which is why retailers screen returns. The 6% hold rate is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Decide failed-inspection case
steps.description: The returns team lead reviews the photos and order, decides whether to refund in full as goodwill, refund partly, or refuse and send the item back to the customer, and records the reason.

error.defect_description: Decision inconsistent with policy.

next.condition: refund in full or in part

evidence.note: Author's estimate of how failed inspections are resolved.

steps.name: Review flagged return for fraud
steps.description: The loss prevention analyst looks at the customer's order and return history, the photos and weights, and linked accounts, and decides to approve, approve with a partial refund or refuse.

error.defect_description: Good customer refused, leading to a complaint.

control.basis: Loss prevention policy: refunds held by fraud rules need analyst review

evidence.note: Fraud share of online returns 10.6% in 2021 (src1); wardrobing described in src6. Decision split is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Release refund or exchange
steps.description: In a daily batch the returns and refunds specialist reviews the processed returns in the order system, releases refunds to the original payment method, creates exchanges where the customer chose one and sends larger refunds for approval.

error.defect_description: Refund issued for the wrong amount or shipping fee refunded against policy.

control.basis: Regulation Z, 12 CFR 1026.12(e): send the credit to the card issuer within 7 business days of accepting a return; card network rules require refunds to the original card

evidence.note: Seven business day limit for merchant credit statements (src4); refund or exchange resolution (src3). The 15% exchange share and batch timing are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Approve high-value refund
steps.description: The customer service supervisor opens each refund above the approval limit, checks it against the inspection grade, photos and order value, and approves it or holds it for questions.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Refund authority limits: refunds above a set amount need a second approver

evidence.note: Approval limits are common internal controls; values are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Card issuer posts the refund
steps.description: The payment processor sends the credit to the customer's card issuer, which posts it to the account; the customer sees it after a few days.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

next.condition: refund rejected, for example a closed card: reissued as store credit

evidence.note: Issuer must credit within 3 business days of receiving the credit statement (src4); processing adds a day or more.

steps.name: Create exchange order
steps.description: The refunds specialist creates a no-charge replacement order for the new size or item in the order system, which goes to the fulfilment queue, and refunds any price difference.

error.defect_description: Wrong size keyed on the replacement order.

evidence.note: Exchanges as a resolution (src3). Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Notify customer of refused return
steps.description: A customer service representative emails or calls the customer to explain why the return was refused, offers to ship the item back, and logs the outcome; some customers escalate.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Assign disposition
steps.description: The returns associate applies the disposition rules to the graded item: back to sellable stock, clean or repair, sell through outlet or liquidator, return to vendor, donate or destroy.

error.defect_description: Sellable item sent to liquidation.

next.condition: liquidate, return to vendor, donate or destroy

evidence.note: Disposition options restock, markdown, refurbish, write-off (src3) and secondary markets (src7). The 72% restock share is the author's estimate for apparel and home goods.

steps.name: Re-pack and put away to sellable stock
steps.description: A stocker re-folds or re-bags and re-labels the item, moves it to its pick location and confirms the put-away in the warehouse system so it can be sold again.

error.defect_description: Item put away to the wrong location.

evidence.note: Restocking as a disposition (src3). Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Stage for liquidation, vendor return or disposal
steps.description: A stocker moves the item to the liquidation, vendor return or disposal area and posts the inventory adjustment in the warehouse system against the disposition code.

error.defect_description: Adjustment posted at the wrong value.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting: inventory write-downs and adjustments posted against approved disposition codes

next.condition: refunded or exchanged; item written down

evidence.note: Secondary markets and write-offs (src3, src7). Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Respond to card dispute
steps.description: When a waiting customer disputes the charge with the card issuer, the payments analyst gathers the order, tracking and return records and answers the dispute in the processor portal, then tells the returns team.

error.defect_description: Response misses the network deadline and the retailer loses the dispute while also refunding.

control.basis: Card network dispute rules (response within the network deadline), accepted in the merchant agreement

evidence.note: Dispute share and handling time are the author's estimates.

exceptions.name: Return handled by customer service
exceptions.description: The customer contacts customer service directly or is outside the portal rules, so an agent creates the authorisation by hand.

exceptions.name: Policy exception requested
exceptions.description: A late or out-of-policy return goes to a supervisor for a goodwill decision.

exceptions.name: New label needed
exceptions.description: The customer loses the label or lets it expire and asks customer service for a new one.

exceptions.name: Never shipped
exceptions.description: The customer does not send the item and the authorisation expires.

exceptions.name: Refund status contact
exceptions.description: The customer calls or chats to ask where the refund is while the parcel is in transit or waiting in the returns backlog.

exceptions.name: Card dispute
exceptions.description: A waiting customer disputes the charge and the payments analyst must answer it.

exceptions.name: Unmatched parcel
exceptions.description: The parcel has no authorisation or contains a different item and goes to the problem shelf for research.

exceptions.name: Failed inspection
exceptions.description: The item is worn, damaged or wrong, so the team lead decides goodwill, partial refund or refusal.

exceptions.name: Fraud review
exceptions.description: Fraud rules hold the refund and a loss prevention analyst reviews it.

exceptions.name: Exchange instead of refund
exceptions.description: The customer asked for another size or item, so an exchange order is created.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from return request to refund posted and item dispositioned
benchmarks.population: Author's estimate for a mid-size online retailer processing returns in its own distribution centre

evidence.note: No source opened measured end-to-end return cycle time. Built from sourced pieces: ground transit of 1 to 5 business days (src5), and the Regulation Z limits of 7 business days to send a credit after accepting a return plus 3 business days for the issuer to post it (src4); customer drop-off delay and warehouse backlog are the author's estimates.

benchmarks.population: 57 US retailers surveyed by NRF and Appriss Retail

benchmarks.unit: share of total US retail sales returned
benchmarks.population: NRF and Appriss Retail retailer surveys

benchmarks.unit: USD lost per 100 USD of returns accepted
benchmarks.population: NRF and Appriss Retail retailer surveys

benchmarks.unit: share of online returns deemed fraudulent (2021)
benchmarks.population: NRF and Appriss Retail retailer survey

evidence.note: Secondary citations (Spaceguard 2021 and unnamed industry data); treat as rough upper bounds.

benchmarks.population: Card refunds in the United States under Regulation Z

evidence.note: Legal maximum, not a measured average.

pain_points.description: Returns wait at the dock and in the returns area for days because outbound orders take priority, especially in January, which delays refunds and triggers status calls.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; the January peak follows the holiday return share in src2.

pain_points.description: Return fraud and abuse such as wardrobing and wrong-item returns cost several dollars per hundred returned, and screening catches only part of it.

evidence.note: $10.30 lost per $100 returned in 2021 and $5.90 in 2020.

pain_points.description: Grading is manual and inconsistent between associates, so sellable items are written down and worn items are refunded.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: About a third of returns still go through customer service, where authorisations are created by hand and errors start.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of channel mix.

pain_points.description: Free return shipping, inspection labour, restocking and lost margin make each return costly even when the item is resold.

evidence.note: Cost components (src3) and cost estimates of up to 5 to 7% of sales (src6, src7).

sources.title: Retail Returns Increased to $761 Billion in 2021 as a Result of Overall Sales Growth
sources.supports: 2021: returns averaged 16.6% of total US retail sales; online return rate 20.8%; about $218 billion of online purchases returned; $10.30 lost to return fraud per $100 of returns accepted; 10.6% of online returns ($23.2 billion) deemed fraudulent; survey of 57 retailers by NRF and Appriss Retail.

sources.title: $428 Billion in Merchandise Returned in 2020
sources.supports: 2020: returns about 10.6% of total US retail sales; online returns more than doubled from 2019; $5.90 lost to return fraud per $100 returned (5.9% fraudulent); 13.3% of holiday sales expected to be returned; survey of 62 retailers.

sources.title: Ecommerce Returns: Rates and Best Practices
sources.publisher: Shopify Enterprise Blog (Elise Dopson and Michael Metcalf)
sources.supports: Return flow: request with reason, rule-based approval, inbound shipment to warehouse or 3PL, inspection and grading, disposition (restock, markdown, refurbish, write-off), refund or exchange, close and inventory update; cost components include return shipping, inspection labour, restocking and lost margin; common reasons fit, not as described, damage, defect, change of mind; bracketing and wardrobing.

sources.title: 12 CFR 1026.12 Special credit card provisions (Regulation Z), paragraph (e)
sources.publisher: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School
sources.supports: A merchant that accepts a return must transmit a credit statement to the card issuer within 7 business days of accepting the return; the issuer must credit the consumer's account within 3 business days of receiving it.

sources.title: FedEx Ground shipping
sources.supports: FedEx Ground delivery within the contiguous US takes 1 to 5 business days; discounted return shipments available to account holders.

sources.title: Product return
sources.supports: Retailers set conditions such as resellable condition, time limits and receipts; some offer only exchange or store credit or charge restocking fees; online sales may see 25 to 40% returns versus 8 to 10% in store (Pacific Standard 2017); returns can cost up to 5% of annual turnover (Spaceguard 2021); wardrobing described.

sources.title: Reverse logistics
sources.supports: Returned goods are quality-checked before returning to inventory, redirected for remanufacturing or sold in secondary markets; return costs cited at up to 7% of gross sales from industry data; about 20% of online purchases returned versus 8 to 10% in store.

sources.title: Return merchandise authorization
sources.supports: A return merchandise authorization is the seller's approval for a product to be returned for refund, replacement or repair and acts as a gatekeeping point.

sources.title: May 2021 National Occupational Employment and Wage Estimates, United States
sources.supports: Median hourly wages: Customer Service Representatives 43-4051 $17.75; First-Line Supervisors of Office and Administrative Support Workers 43-1011 $29.13; Shipping, Receiving and Inventory Clerks 43-5071 $17.74; Laborers and Freight, Stock and Material Movers, Hand 53-7062 $15.02; Stockers and Order Fillers 53-7065 $14.48; First-Line Supervisors of Transportation and Material Moving Workers 53-1047 $26.37; Compliance Officers 13-1041 $34.45; Bookkeeping, Accounting and Auditing Clerks 43-3031 $21.90.

sources.title: Employer Costs for Employee Compensation - December 2021 (news release)
sources.supports: Retail trade: total compensation $22.69 per hour, wages and salaries $17.42 (76.8%), benefits $5.27 (23.2%).

assumptions: One case is one return request for one or more items from one order; the warehouse handles the items of one request together.
Customer and carrier time is modelled as waits with zero staff touch time.
Refunds are released after inspection in a daily batch; some retailers refund on the first carrier scan, which shortens the customer's wait by four to ten days.

The disposition and put-away steps run in parallel with the refund in practice; they are listed after it with short waits and named in concurrent_with, so the simulated cycle runs to the end of disposition.
The cycle_time_days benchmark is the author's estimate assembled from sourced transit and refund-timing limits; no source opened measured it.
Loaded hourly cost is the BLS May 2021 national median wage for the nearest SOC code times 1.45 (1.30 benefits from BLS ECEC December 2021 for retail trade, about 1.12 overhead by author estimate).
Channel mix, hold rates, failed-inspection and fraud-review rates, exchange share and handle times are tier C estimates.
